comments.content: The test uses `#[tokio::test]` but the rest of this file appears to use `#[test]`. Verify that `tokio` is available as a dev-dependency with the `macros` and `rt` features enabled for the `uv` crate's tests; otherwise this test will fail to compile.

The mock server is started with `MockServer::start().await` but never explicitly shut down. While `MockServer` shuts down on drop, the test is `async` and the server is held across `.await` points; ensure the server is dropped before the test ends (it is, at end of scope) — no action needed, but consider using `MockServer::start()` with a guard if flakiness is observed.

Two mocks are registered for the same `GET /requirements.txt` path: one requiring basic auth (200) and one without (401). Wiremock matches mocks in registration order, so the first (auth-required) mock will match when credentials are present, and the second will match otherwise. This works, but is fragile — if the first mock's matcher is ever loosened, the 401 mock becomes unreachable. Consider using `.with_priority()` or a single mock with a custom responder to make the intent explicit.

The second `Mock::given(...).mount(&server)` for the updated `requirements.txt` is added on top of the existing mocks. Since wiremock matches in registration order, the earlier 200 mock (without content-type) will still match first and the new mock will never be hit. This means the test does not actually exercise the updated body. Use `server.reset().await` before mounting the new mock, or use `MockServer::register` with priorities.

The snapshot for the failing case truncates the URL at `http://[LOCALHOST]` because the filter `127\.0\.0\.1[^\r\n]*` matches greedily up to end of line. This hides the actual error message (e.g., 401 status). Consider narrowing the filter so the error detail remains visible, e.g. `127\.0\.0\.1:\d+`.
